PP.PracticalTools.Enabled.Name: Practical tools: Trade bonus
PP.PracticalTools.Enabled.Hint: A practical trade tool (Practical quality) grants +1 SL on a failed Trade test when the specialisation in the tool's name (in parentheses) matches the skill's specialisation. A parenthesis containing "any" / "*" (or Polish "dowolne") matches any specialisation.
PP.Artistic.Enabled.Name: Artistic talent: Art in Career
PP.Artistic.Enabled.Hint: The Artistic talent adds the character's Art skill to the current Career (advanced at the normal XP cost); if Art is already in the Career, each Advance costs 5 XP less. The character must own the Art skill with a chosen specialisation. Changing this requires a reload.
PP.Poison.Enabled.Name: Poisoned: Endurance Test at end of Round
PP.Poison.Enabled.Hint: At the end of every Round (or Turn, if the system counts Poisoned per Turn) a poisoned character gets a chat reminder with buttons: Endurance Test (Challenging +0) and Heal Test (another character). Success removes 1 Poisoned Condition + 1 per SL.
PP.Poison.Mode.Name: Poisoned: test dialog opening
PP.Poison.Mode.Hint: When the Endurance Test dialog should open by itself. The chat card with buttons is always posted.
PP.Poison.Unconscious.Name: Poisoned: unconsciousness and death (TB)
PP.Poison.Unconscious.Hint: A poisoned character at 0 Wounds falls Unconscious after a number of Rounds equal to their Toughness Bonus. Poisoned and Unconscious — after another TB Rounds they make an Endurance Test; failure means death. When the next test comes after a success — see "Poisoned: further death tests".
PP.Poison.DeathMode.Name: Poisoned: further death tests
PP.Poison.DeathMode.Hint: The first Endurance Test against death always comes after TB Rounds Unconscious while Poisoned. This setting decides when the next one comes after a successful test. Only works with unconsciousness and death (TB) enabled.
PP.Poison.DeathMode.Round: Every Round (next test in the following Round)
PP.Poison.DeathMode.Sl: After 1 + SL Rounds (SL of the successful test)
PP.Poison.Overflow.Name: Poisoned: excess SL without Fatigue
PP.Poison.Overflow.Hint: When a successful Endurance or Heal Test removes more Conditions than the character has (1 + SL > Poisoned level), Poisoned is removed without Fatigue — like the system does with an excess. Off = rulebook (always Fatigued once cured).
PP.Poison.CuredOverflow: {name}: Poisoned removed (−{n}) — excess SL, no Fatigue.
PP.Poison.Reminder: End of Round — you may attempt an Endurance Test (Challenging +0). Success removes 1 Poisoned Condition + 1 per SL. A Heal Test by another character works the same.
PP.Poison.FellUnconscious: {name} has spent {tb} Round(s) at 0 Wounds while Poisoned and falls Unconscious.
PP.Poison.UncCounter: Unconscious while Poisoned: Round {n}/{due} — Endurance Test after {due} Rounds, failure = death.
PP.Poison.DeathDue: {name}: Unconscious while Poisoned — Endurance Test against death! Failure means death.
PP.Poison.DeathFailed: {name} fails the Endurance Test and dies horribly from the poison.
PP.Poison.DeathSurvived: {name} fights the poison — another test in {n} Round(s) if still Poisoned and Unconscious.
PP.Poison.Cured: {name}: Poisoned removed (−{n}). The character gains a Fatigued Condition.
PP.Poison.NoHealer: Select the token of the character making the Heal Test (or assign yourself a character).
PP.Poison.NotOwner: You do not own this character.
PP.Poison.AlreadyTested: This test has already been made this Round.
PP.Stunned.Mode.Name: Stunned: reminder at start of Turn
PP.Stunned.Mode.Hint: At the start of a Stunned character's Turn (in combat), a reminder that they cannot take Actions. Chat card: public for player characters, whispered to the GM for NPCs. The notification pops up for the owning player (NPCs: for the GM). If the Turn starts a new Round and the Endurance Test dialog opened automatically, the reminder comes after the test (if still Stunned).
PP.Stunned.Title: Stunned {n}
PP.Stunned.Card: Start of Turn — {name}: no Action this Turn. May Move at half speed and defend in Opposed Tests (but not with Language (Magick)). Penalty to all Tests (−10 per Condition); melee attackers gain +1 Advantage before rolling.
PP.Stunned.Popup: {name} — Stunned: no Action this Turn (half Movement and defending only).
PP.Stunned.Test.Name: Stunned: Endurance Test at end of Round
PP.Stunned.Test.Hint: At the end of every Round a Stunned character may attempt a Challenging (+0) Endurance Test: success removes 1 Stunned Condition + 1 per SL, and once all are removed the character gains a Fatigued Condition (unless already Fatigued). The chat card with a button is always posted (unless Off); this setting decides whether the test dialog opens by itself. If the active Condition definition (the system's English one) has its own test, the module does not duplicate it.
PP.Stunned.Overflow.Name: Stunned: excess SL without Fatigue
PP.Stunned.Overflow.Hint: When a successful Endurance Test removes more Conditions than the character has (1 + SL > Stunned level), Stunned is removed without Fatigue — like the system's own test. Off = rulebook (Fatigued unless already Fatigued).
PP.Stunned.CuredOverflow: {name}: Stunned removed (−{n}) — excess SL, no Fatigue.
PP.Stunned.Name: Stunned
PP.Stunned.EndRound: End of Round — you may attempt an Endurance Test (Challenging +0). Success removes 1 Stunned Condition + 1 per SL.
PP.Stunned.Cured: {name}: Stunned removed (−{n}). The character gains a Fatigued Condition.
PP.Stunned.CuredNoFatigue: {name}: Stunned removed (−{n}). Already Fatigued — no additional Condition.
PP.Stunned.NotOwner: You do not own this character.
PP.Stunned.AlreadyTested: This test has already been made this Round.
PP.Slash.Enabled.Name: Slash: Bleeding on a Critical Wound
PP.Slash.Enabled.Hint: A weapon with the Slash (X) quality that causes a Critical Wound (critical attack roll or damage to 0 Wounds) gives the victim 1 Bleeding Condition and posts a chat card.
PP.Slash.Advantage.Name: Slash: Advantage button
PP.Slash.Advantage.Hint: A button on the Slash card: the attacker spends X Advantage and the opponent gains 1 additional Bleeding Condition (once per hit).
PP.Slash.Name: Slash
PP.Slash.Description: Slashing weapons focus their cutting edge to leave open wounds. If the weapon causes a Critical Wound, in addition to all other effects of the Critical Wound the victim also gains 1 Bleeding Condition. You may spend X Advantage to give your opponent 1 additional Bleeding Condition.
PP.Slash.Title: Slash ({x})
PP.Slash.Spent: {attacker} spends Advantage ({x}): {defender} gains 1 additional Bleeding Condition.
PP.Slash.Used: Advantage for Slash has already been spent on this hit.
PP.Slash.NotOwner: Only the owner of the attacking character can spend the Advantage.
PP.Slash.NoGM: An active GM is required to apply Bleeding.
PP.Give.Enabled.Name: Give money: /give command
PP.Give.Enabled.Hint: A player types /give <amount> split=N reason=... — the money is taken from their character and a chat card with N shares appears for other players to claim (like the GM's /credit). Requires an active GM.
PP.Give.CommandDescription: Give money from your character for others to claim in chat.
PP.Give.CommandNotes: The amount is taken from your character and divided into split equal shares (default 1). Any remainder stays with you. You cannot claim your own share.
PP.Give.Disabled: The /give command is disabled in the Podstawowy+ module settings.
PP.Give.NoCharacter: You have no assigned character to give money from.
PP.Give.NoGM: An active GM is required for money to be claimed.
PP.Give.TooSmall: The amount is too small to divide into {n} shares.
PP.Give.Remainder: The remainder ({rest}) stays in your purse.
